The two TES units were connected using the designed pipe. Hydronic loop sensors, including flowmeters, temperature sensors, and pressure transducers, were installed around each component. The two TES units were connected to the modified rooftop heat pump unit using a commercially available brazed-plate heat exchanger (Figure 89). Modified RTU TES unit installations/connections Figure 89: Field-test site installed: Modified HP RTU (left) and TES installed & hydronic loop piping, including flow meters and connection of TES completed and ready for test systems installation/connection The field test instrumentation plan was constructed to ensure that all necessary data was available for the following purposes: • Quantify system performance (COP, power requirements, capacities) during all hours of the day • Quantify the demand reduction capability of the HP-TES during peak hours • Utilize the sensor data for system troubleshooting and HP-TES model validation Consequently, sensors were placed in the modified HP RTU, the TES hydronic loop, and indoor spaces (Figure 90). Within the RTU, the sensors include power meters for the fans and the compressor, refrigerant temperatures and pressures, and indoor coil supply and return air temperatures and relative humidities. Additionally, outdoor air temperatures were measured to evaluate the system's demand-reduction capabilities at different operating temperatures. Within the hydronic loops, a power meter was installed on the loop pump, and flow, temperature, and pressure sensors were placed around each component to measure heat transfer, pressure drop, and the TES state of charge. Indoor sensors were installed to determine instantaneous building loads and ensure that the thermostat setpoint conditions were met.
